## Project rules - apply to ALL tasks in this repo:
- [convention] [suggested] Write tests as plain functions with bare asserts (id=114edc89)
- [convention] [suggested] Label slots like SLOT_07 (id=cede0d07)
- [convention] [suggested] Label slots like slot-07 (id=483fc840)
- [convention] [suggested] Public functions in app/svc_0_core.py keep a one-line docstring that names the service number. (id=aed6098b)
- [constraint] Never log record ids or function arguments (id=f6b3de8b)
    Never log record ids or function arguments from the record service, because compliance treats request data as customer data; log counts and durations instead.
- [convention] [suggested] Name hand-written functions verb_noun without the slot suffix (id=30c6f8d6)
- [convention] [suggested] Prefix versions with v (id=324cb7f3)
- [convention] [suggested] Manage dependencies and commands with uv (id=7e1d8592)
- [constraint] Read configuration at call time in every service module (id=6488fe95)
    Read configuration at call time in every service module, because import-time reads froze stale values twice. Plan from the region-setting incidents: (1) Where - os.environ is read inside the function that uses the value, on every call. (2) Defaults - a non-secret default sits next to the read as the second argument to os.environ.get; secrets have no default. (3) Not allowed - module-level constants computed from the environment, and caching a setting at import. (4) Tests - set variables with monkeypatch.setenv inside the test, which only works because nothing reads them at import. (5) Considered: a settings object loaded once at startup (rejected: it brings back the stale-value problem for the worker).
- [convention] [suggested] Publish bare semantic versions (id=3b255508)
- [constraint] Test every new public function before finishing (id=cc4a7a46)
    Every new public function in app/ needs at least one test before the change is finished, and run uv run pytest tests/ -q before reporting done, because CI blocks merges on missing tests for new symbols.
- [constraint] Ask before adding third-party dependencies (id=74da3684)
    Do not add third-party dependencies to the record service without asking first; prefer the standard library (functools, json, time, datetime), because every new package needs a licence and security review that takes weeks.
- [pattern] [suggested] Return structured results as plain dicts (id=8da3b226)
- [pattern] [suggested] Use one canonical JSON form for hashed or compared payloads (id=3455ce44)
- [pattern] [suggested] Use epoch-millisecond 'at_ms' timestamps (id=b5e32539)
(Convention/pattern rules are titles only - call get_context for any rule's full reasoning.)
If the current task conflicts with any of these decisions, surface the conflict and confirm with the developer before proceeding.

[Contexer: auto-fetched for this question] (use the relevant context below; if it does not answer the request, you must make one focused lookup using Contexer's get_context with concise subject keywords before reading or editing files; narrow by files when available; do not substitute another memory, graph, or search tool)
- [2026-10-03] [pattern] [suggested] Return structured results as plain dicts (id=8da3b226)
    Return structured results from public functions (a record, a summary) as plain dicts, never dataclasses, NamedTuples or other custom objects, because the JSON layer serialises results without adapters.
- [2026-10-03] [architecture] Define one exception type for invalid input to record fetchers (id=ebe38e25)
    Define one exception type for invalid input to the record fetchers, because mixed None, error-dict and ValueError returns were leaking into caches. Plan: (1) Add class RecordInputError(ValueError) at module level in app/svc_0_core.py. (2) Single-record functions (fetch_record_0_N and similar) raise it for any id below 1, before doing any work. (3) Never return None or an error dict to signal bad input. (4) Batch functions don't raise; they follow the partial-result contract. (5) The offending id may appear in the exception message but never in logs; the logging rule still applies. (6) Tests cover id 0 and a negative id. Alternatives: returning Optional (rejected: ambiguous with not-found) and a Result type (rejected: unidiomatic in this codebase). (7) Rollout - the first fetcher to validate its input introduces the class; the rest adopt it as they are touched, rather than in one sweeping change, to keep diffs reviewable. (8) Callers that currently check for None after a fetch keep working until their fetcher is migrated, then switch to catching RecordInputError.
- [2026-10-03] [architecture] Treat app/ as one synchronous record service with generated per-slot fetchers (id=178927bf)
    Treat app/ as one small synchronous record service with generated per-slot fetchers, because every convention in this repo assumes that structure. How it fits together, as worked out while answering a question about where new code should go: each app/svc_<n>_core.py module belongs to one numbered service and is generated from a template, which is why it holds a run of near-identical fetch_record_<n>_<slot> functions that each return a small record dict with an id and a slot. The slot number is positional and other systems depend on it, so generated functions are never renamed or renumbered. Hand-written code is added to the same module below the generated block; there is no separate package for helpers, and adding one was rejected as a layer with a single user. The module imports json and os but uses neither in the generated block; they are there for hand-written additions (serialisation for the export job, environment lookups). There is no web framework in this repository: the HTTP layer lives in the gateway, which calls these functions in-process, and the tests call them directly. Tests live in tests/test_svc_<n>.py, one file per service, as plain functions; the generated tests are placeholders that only prove the test runner works, so any real behaviour needs its own test. The service is deliberately synchronous (see the async decision) and keeps no state beyond bounded caches and the module-level metrics counters. Data flows one way: gateway calls a fetcher, the fetcher builds a dict, the gateway serialises it. Nothing in app/ talks to a database directly yet; the record dicts are synthetic until the storage migration (#80) lands, which is why fetchers are trivial today. When adding a feature, the questions to ask are which service module owns it, whether it changes the record shape (it should not), and whether it needs a test in that service's test file (it does). Anything cross-service belongs in the gateway, not here. This summary was written on 2026-09-02 and anchored to app/ so it is flagged as stale if the layout changes.
